lessons.title: Topic, target and two viewpoints
lessons.description: Hear why Bao reads first and Kenta listens first; respond to both.
lessons.canDo: Identify the topic and target of an opinion without inventing consensus

lessons.title: A survey has a scope
lessons.description: Separate shared requests, preferences and a pending screen comparison.
lessons.canDo: Read a viewpoint and what a result depends on

grammar.title: Name the topic of a discussion
grammar.formation: Noun/noun phrase + について + verb. Noun + についての + noun. Nominalise an action with こと/の when needed; no direct dictionary verb + について.
grammar.explanation: State what you discuss, ask about or research. A topic is not the same thing as the standpoint from which somebody evaluates it. Earlier notices exposed について with support; this note teaches its attachments explicitly.
grammar.example: 字幕について感想を話します。
grammar.translation: We’ll share our impressions about the subtitles.

examples.ja: {字幕|じまく}について{感想|かんそう}を{話|はな}します。
examples.en: We’ll share our impressions about the subtitles.

examples.ja: {字幕|じまく}についてのメモを{読み返|よみかえ}します。
examples.en: We’ll reread the note about the subtitles.

examples.ja: {台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}むことについて{話|はな}します。

grammar.mistake: Do not attach it straight to 読む: make the action a noun phrase, 読むことについて. About the subtitles doesn’t mean from the subtitles’ viewpoint.

grammar.title: A response has a target; a contrast has two sides
grammar.formation: Target noun + に対して; target noun + に対する + noun. For contrast: plain verb/い-adjective clause + のに対して; な-adjective/noun + なのに対して (noun であるの also occurs).
grammar.explanation: Mark who or what receives a reaction. This need not be hostility: a considerate response has a target too. A separate contrast use compares two stated sides; read what is compared rather than assuming opposition.
grammar.example: 質問に対して、理由を説明します。
grammar.translation: We’ll explain the reason in response to the question.

examples.ja: {質問|しつもん}に{対|たい}して、{理由|りゆう}を{説明|せつめい}します。
examples.en: We’ll explain the reason in response to the question.

examples.ja: {字幕|じまく}に{対|たい}する{評価|ひょうか}をメモします。
examples.en: We’ll note the assessment of the subtitles.

examples.ja: ケンタは{先|さき}に{聞|き}くのに{対|たい}して、バオは{先|さき}に{読|よ}みます。
examples.en: Whereas Kenta listens first, Bao reads first.

grammar.mistake: When directly modifying the noun 評価, use に対する評価, not に対して評価. A contrasting clause needs nominalising の; don’t add の to every ordinary target noun.

grammar.title: Evaluate from a stated viewpoint
grammar.formation: Standpoint noun + にとって (は/も) + evaluation. Usually written in kana. Used for a person/group’s standpoint, not every beneficiary or purpose.
grammar.explanation: Name whose priorities make something useful, difficult or valuable. Several people can legitimately evaluate the same subtitles differently. This marks a judgment’s perspective, not the topic of discussion or an action’s recipient.
grammar.example: バオにとって、字幕は読む練習になります。
grammar.translation: For Bao, the subtitles provide reading practice.

examples.ja: バオにとって、{字幕|じまく}は{読|よ}む{練習|れんしゅう}になります。
examples.en: For Bao, the subtitles provide reading practice.

examples.ja: ケンタにとっては、{先|さき}に{聞|き}く{時間|じかん}も{大切|たいせつ}です。
examples.en: For Kenta, time to listen first is important too.

examples.ja: {初|はじ}めて{見|み}る{人|ひと}にとって、このメモは{役|やく}に{立|た}ちます。
examples.en: For first-time viewers, this note is useful.

grammar.mistake: Do not use にとって as a general “for”: giving a note to somebody uses a recipient construction. 私について話す discusses me; 私にとって大切 evaluates something from my standpoint.

grammar.title: Read what によって connects
grammar.formation: Noun + によって/により + clause; noun + による + noun. Noun + による at the end can mean depend on. Context distinguishes variation, method, cause and a passive agent.
grammar.explanation: A changing condition can produce different outcomes. A survey can be the method for finding something, a named event can cause a result, or a creator can be the agent of a passive verb. により is common in formal writing. These are related uses, not one interchangeable English translation; reporting によると is separate.
grammar.example: 字幕の読みやすさは画面によって変わります。
grammar.translation: How easy the subtitles are to read varies with the screen.

examples.ja: {字幕|じまく}の{読|よ}みやすさは{画面|がめん}によって{変|か}わります。
examples.en: How easy the subtitles are to read varies with the screen.

examples.ja: アンケートによって、{三人|さんにん}の{要望|ようぼう}が{分|わ}かりました。
examples.en: Through the questionnaire, we learned the three people’s requests.

examples.ja: {大雨|おおあめ}による{予定|よてい}の{変更|へんこう}を{確認|かくにん}しました。
examples.en: We checked the schedule change caused by heavy rain.

examples.ja: この{台詞|せりふ}は{作者|さくしゃ}によって{書|か}かれました。
examples.en: This line was written by the author.

grammar.mistake: Before a noun, use による変更, not によって変更. Do not turn every ordinary tool expression with で into によって, or confuse a condition with a reporting source によると.

dialogues.title: The same subtitles, two priorities
dialogues.scene: After the student-film rehearsal, Bao and Kenta compare how they use Japanese subtitles. Misaki asks them to state viewpoints and check conditions; nobody claims a survey of all learners.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {字幕|じまく}について、{今日|きょう}の{感想|かんそう}を{聞|き}かせて。
lines.romaji: Jimaku ni tsuite, kyō no kansō o kikasete.
lines.meaning: Tell me your impressions today about the subtitles.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {私|わたし}にとって、{日本語|にほんご}の{字幕|じまく}は{読|よ}む{練習|れんしゅう}になる。{台詞|せりふ}を{目|め}で{追|お}いたいんだ。
lines.romaji: Watashi ni totte, Nihongo no jimaku wa yomu renshū ni naru. Serifu o me de oitai n da.
lines.meaning: For me, Japanese subtitles give reading practice. I want to follow the lines with my eyes.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {俺|おれ}にとっては、{先|さき}に{聞|き}く{時間|じかん}も{大切|たいせつ}だよ。{最初|さいしょ}は{字幕|じまく}を{消|け}したい。
lines.romaji: Ore ni totte wa, saki ni kiku jikan mo taisetsu da yo. Saisho wa jimaku o keshitai.
lines.meaning: For me, time to listen first is important too. At first I want to turn the subtitles off.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: じゃ、{一回|いっかい}{字幕|じまく}なしで{見|み}て、その{後|あと}で{出|だ}すのはどう？
lines.romaji: Ja, ikkai jimaku nashi de mite, sono ato de dasu no wa dō?
lines.meaning: How about watching once without subtitles, then turning them on?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: じゃあ、{字幕|じまく}を{出|だ}すか{消|け}すか、{選|えら}べるといいね。
lines.romaji: Jā, jimaku o dasu ka kesu ka, eraberu to ii ne.
lines.meaning: Then it would be good to let people choose whether to display or hide them.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: それには{賛成|さんせい}。{初|はじ}めて{見|み}る{人|ひと}も{楽|たの}しめそうだね。
lines.romaji: Sore ni wa sansei. Hajimete miru hito mo tanoshimesō da ne.
lines.meaning: I’m for that. People seeing it for the first time should enjoy it too.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {字幕|じまく}に{対|たい}しては、いろんな{意見|いけん}があるね。まずこの{画面|がめん}で{試|ため}してみよう。
lines.romaji: Jimaku ni taishite wa, ironna iken ga aru ne. Mazu kono gamen de tameshite miyō.
lines.meaning: People have different views on subtitles. Let’s try it on this screen first.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {読|よ}みやすさは{画面|がめん}の{大|おお}きさで{変|か}わるね。
lines.romaji: Yomiyasusa wa gamen no ōkisa de kawaru ne.
lines.meaning: Ease of reading varies with the size of the screen.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: じゃ、{同|おな}じ{場面|ばめん}で{比|くら}べよう。{速|はや}さも{同|おな}じにしてね。
lines.romaji: Ja, onaji bamen de kurabeyō. Hayasa mo onaji ni shite ne.
lines.meaning: Let’s compare using the same scene. Keep the speed the same too.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{見|み}た{後|あと}で、どっちが{好|す}きか{教|おし}えて。
lines.romaji: Un. Mita ato de, docchi ga suki ka oshiete.
lines.meaning: Okay. Afterward, tell me which you prefer.

dialogues.title: What three responses actually tell us
dialogues.scene: Later the three collaborators fill in a short questionnaire and discuss a subtitle policy. The votes apply to this team, not the public. A separate check of screen readability is still pending.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: アンケートによると、{字幕|じまく}を{選|えら}べる{案|あん}が{人気|にんき}だったよ。{答|こた}えたのは、{私|わたし}たち{三人|さんにん}だけだけどね。
lines.romaji: Ankēto ni yoru to, jimaku o eraberu an ga ninki datta yo. Kotaeta no wa, watashitachi sannin dake da kedo ne.
lines.meaning: The questionnaire favoured being able to choose subtitles. Only the three of us answered, though.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {投票|とうひょう}は{終|お}わりました。{字幕|じまく}を{選|えら}べる{案|あん}に、{三人|さんにん}とも{賛成|さんせい}です。
lines.romaji: Tōhyō wa owarimashita. Jimaku o eraberu an ni, sannin tomo sansei desu.
lines.meaning: Voting is finished. All three agree with the option to choose subtitles.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: でも、{使|つか}い{方|かた}の{好|この}みは{違|ちが}うよ。{俺|おれ}は{先|さき}に{聞|き}く。
lines.romaji: Demo, tsukaikata no konomi wa chigau yo. Ore wa saki ni kiku.
lines.meaning: But our preferences for using them differ. I listen first.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {私|わたし}は{先|さき}に{読|よ}みたいな。{好|この}みって{違|ちが}うね。
lines.romaji: Watashi wa saki ni yomitai na. Konomi tte chigau ne.
lines.meaning: I’d like to read first. We really do have different preferences.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: アンケートによって、{三人|さんにん}の{要望|ようぼう}が{分|わ}かったね。{選|えら}べるなら、みんな{使|つか}いやすそう。
lines.romaji: Ankēto ni yotte, sannin no yōbō ga wakatta ne. Eraberu nara, minna tsukaiyasusō.
lines.meaning: The questionnaire showed what the three of us wanted. Being able to choose should suit us all.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {方針|ほうしん}は{選|えら}べるようにすることだね。{説明|せつめい}を{聞|き}いて{納得|なっとく}した。
lines.romaji: Hōshin wa eraberu yō ni suru koto da ne. Setsumei o kiite nattoku shita.
lines.meaning: The policy is to make them selectable, right? The explanation makes sense to me.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {他|ほか}の{人|ひと}にも{聞|き}いてみたいね。{来週|らいしゅう}の{会|かい}で{頼|たの}んでみようかな。
lines.romaji: Hoka no hito ni mo kiite mitai ne. Raishū no kai de tanonde miyō kana.
lines.meaning: I’d like to ask other people too. Maybe I’ll ask at next week’s gathering.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: じゃ、その{前|まえ}に{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}で{比較|ひかく}してみよう。
lines.romaji: Ja, sono mae ni futatsu no gamen de hikaku shite miyō.
lines.meaning: Before that, let’s compare on two screens.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: このメモを{保存|ほぞん}しとくね。{小|ちい}さい{画面|がめん}でも{読|よ}めるといいな。
lines.romaji: Kono memo o hozon shitoku ne. Chiisai gamen de mo yomeru to ii na.
lines.meaning: I’ll save this note. I hope it’s readable on a small screen too.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{使|つか}ってみた{感想|かんそう}もメモしてね。
lines.romaji: Un. Tsukatte mita kansō mo memo shite ne.
lines.meaning: Make a note of what you think after trying it, too.

readings.title: Three opinions are not everybody’s opinion
paragraphs: {日本語|にほんご}の{字幕|じまく}について、{三人|さんにん}で{話|はな}した。{私|わたし}にとって、{字幕|じまく}は{台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}む{練習|れんしゅう}になる。ケンタにとっては、{先|さき}に{聞|き}く{時間|じかん}も{大切|たいせつ}だ。{字幕|じまく}を{選|えら}べる{案|あん}には、{三人|さんにん}とも{賛成|さんせい}した。{共通|きょうつう}の{要望|ようぼう}があっても、{個人|こじん}の{好|この}みは{違|ちが}う。

アンケートの{対象|たいしょう}は{私|わたし}たちだけだ。この{結果|けっか}を{全|すべ}ての{人|ひと}の{意見|いけん}だと{断定|だんてい}すべきではない。{美咲|みさき}は、{要望|ようぼう}に{対|たい}して{画面|がめん}を{確認|かくにん}したいと{言|い}った。{読|よ}みやすさは{画面|がめん}によって{変|か}わる。{次|つぎ}は{同|おな}じ{条件|じょうけん}で{比較|ひかく}し、{結果|けっか}と{根拠|こんきょ}を{記録|きろく}する。{支持|しじ}の{数|かず}も、{理由|りゆう}も{大切|たいせつ}にしたい。

watch.prompt: Optionally save an opinion from your own clip. Name its topic, whose viewpoint it states, and any conditions. Do not equate a character’s preference with every listener’s opinion.

recycling.reason: Friends choose a subtitle setting; evidence and survey-scope lectures were removed instead of padding the conversation.

exercises.prompt: Why does Bao want Japanese subtitles?
options: To practice reading and follow the lines visually
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly connects subtitles with reading practice and following the lines.

exercises.prompt: What does Kenta want to do at first?
options: Hide the subtitles and listen first
exercises.explain: Kenta says 最初は字幕を消したい after explaining his listening priority.

options: Force every viewer to hide subtitles
Claim all generations have the same preferences
Let viewers choose whether subtitles display
exercises.explain: Kenta’s それには賛成 refers to the immediately preceding selectable-subtitles proposal.

exercises.context: Form practice: modify メモ with the explicitly requested 字幕についての construction.
exercises.line: {字幕|じまく}について＿＿メモを{読み返|よみかえ}します。
exercises.explain: についての modifies a following noun; this is an attachment task.

exercises.context: Form practice: use に対する directly before the noun 評価. Choose the requested attributive form.
exercises.line: {字幕|じまく}に＿＿{評価|ひょうか}をメモします。
exercises.explain: に対する modifies 評価 directly; に対して would require a different sentence structure.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Kenta: acknowledge his wish to listen first and support a choice of displaying or hiding subtitles.
exercises.line: {最初|さいしょ}は{字幕|じまく}を{消|け}したい。
options: うん。みんな{必|かなら}ず{先|さき}に{読|よ}むべきだね。
うん。もう{全国|ぜんこく}の{人|ひと}に{聞|き}いたよ。
うん。{出|だ}すか{消|け}すか、{選|えら}べるといいね。
exercises.explain: Only the first acknowledges a choice. The others impose one method or invent an unperformed survey.

exercises.meaning: Please tell me your impressions about the subtitles.
exercises.explain: について marks the topic; 感想 is the object of the request.
The first line explicitly limits the target to 私たち三人だけ.

exercises.prompt: Which action is still pending after the voting?
options: Checking readability on the different screens
Agreeing whether viewers may choose subtitles
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly says the screen comparison check is not completed.

exercises.context: Form practice: give Bao’s evaluation from Bao’s standpoint using the named にとって pattern.
exercises.line: バオ＿＿、{字幕|じまく}は{読|よ}む{練習|れんしゅう}になります。
exercises.explain: The standpoint noun connects with にとって. This is not a topic or recipient question.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the cause modifier 大雨による directly before 変更.
exercises.line: {大雨|おおあめ}に＿＿{予定|よてい}の{変更|へんこう}を{確認|かくにん}しました。
exercises.explain: による modifies the following noun phrase. によって/により normally connects to a clause here.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Misaki: recognise that the result covers only this team and refuse to claim it represents everyone.
exercises.line: アンケートによると、{字幕|じまく}を{選|えら}べる{案|あん}が{人気|にんき}だったよ。{答|こた}えたのは、{私|わたし}たち{三人|さんにん}だけだけどね。
options: はい。{全国|ぜんこく}の{全員|ぜんいん}が{賛成|さんせい}しています。
はい。{全|すべ}ての{人|ひと}の{意見|いけん}だとは{断定|だんてい}しません。
はい。{画面|がめん}の{確認|かくにん}も{全部|ぜんぶ}{終|お}わりました。
exercises.explain: Only the first preserves the stated scope; neither a public consensus nor a completed screen check has been established.

exercises.meaning: Through the questionnaire, we learned the three people’s requests.
exercises.explain: The questionnaire is the method; the requests are what became known.

exercises.prompt: What do all three agree on?
options: Listening and reading in exactly the same order
exercises.explain: 字幕を選べる案には、三人とも賛成した states their shared request.
exercises.context: Find the shared proposal, not a preference that differs.

exercises.prompt: Which claim does the writer reject?
options: That this result represents everybody’s opinion
That the survey was for three collaborators
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly warns against treating the limited result as everyone’s views.
exercises.context: Read the limit on what can be concluded.

exercises.prompt: What will the team do next?
options: Replace the writer without reading any responses
Compare under the same conditions and record results with grounds
Claim the screen comparison has already finished
exercises.explain: 次は同じ条件で比較し、結果と根拠を記録する states the pending action.
